item.title: AstraZeneca Camizestrant FDA Delay
item.description:
• Summary: The FDA has delayed its decision on camizestrant (AZD9833), AstraZeneca's oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) for advanced breast cancer, following a negative advisory committee vote. The panel raised concerns about the drug's efficacy and safety profile compared to existing therapies. Camizestrant is being developed for estrogen receptor-positive (ER+) breast cancer, a common subtype. The delay extends the review period, with a new decision date expected later in 2026. The news impacted AstraZeneca's stock and the broader oncology sector.
  • MoAs: Camizestrant is a next-generation oral SERD that binds to and degrades the estrogen receptor, blocking estrogen signaling that drives tumor growth in ER+ breast cancer.
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, ApexOnco, Fierce Pharma, Fierce Biotech, Endpoints News

item.title: Akeso Ivonescimab ASCO Preview
item.description:
• Summary: Ahead of the American Society of Clinical Oncology (ASCO) 2026 annual meeting, attention is on Akeso's ivonescimab (PD-1/VEGF bispecific antibody). The drug is expected to present pivotal data from a Phase 3 trial in first-line non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Ivonescimab is designed to simultaneously block PD-1 and VEGF pathways, potentially improving efficacy over standard PD-1 inhibitors. Analysts anticipate high-stakes evaluation of the data, as positive results could position ivonescimab as a new standard of care. Akeso's stock has rallied on the excitement.
  • MoAs: Bispecific antibody that targets both PD-1 on T cells (checkpoint inhibition) and VEGF (anti-angiogenesis), combining two mechanisms to enhance anti-tumor immune response and inhibit tumor vascularization.
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma

item.title: Kura Oncology Cancer Drug
item.description:
• Summary: Kura Oncology has reported encouraging clinical data for its lead drug ziftomenib, a menin inhibitor targeting acute myeloid leukemia, potentially unlocking a $2 billion market opportunity.
  • MoAs: Menin inhibitor
  • Sources: BioSpace

item.title: Waypoint Bio CAR-T Trials in China
item.description:

  • MoAs: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapy (CAR-T)
  • Sources: Endpoints News
